nodes.name: Monolayer 1T-MoS2 hollow structure synthesis
nodes.procedure: Well-defined monolayer 1T-MoS2 hollow structures were synthesized using previously established method [29] (see Figures S1 and S2, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: Well-defined monolayer 1T-MoS2 hollow structures (Figures S1 and S2, Supporting Information) were synthesized as supports using our previously established method.[29]

nodes.name: Wet-chemical noble metal growth on 1T-MoS2
nodes.procedure: A mild wet-chemical synthesis was employed to in situ grow noble metals (M=Pt, Rh, Ru) on the obtained 1T-MoS2 surface, yielding 1T-MoS2@M (M=Pt, Rh, Ru) heterostructures.
nodes.source_text: Subsequently, a mild wet-chemical synthesis was employed to in situ grow noble metals (M=Pt, Rh, Ru) on the obtained 1T-MoS2 surface, yielding 1T-MoS2@M (M=Pt, Rh, Ru) heterostructures (Figure 1a).

nodes.name: 2H-MoS2@Pt synthesis via phase conversion
nodes.procedure: 1T-MoS2 was thermally converted to 2H-MoS2 via annealing under N2 at 800°C. Subsequently, Pt subnanodots (SNDs) were in situ grown on the 2H-MoS2 using the same wet-chemical synthesis approach as for 1T-MoS2@Pt, forming 2H-MoS2@Pt heterostructure (Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information).
nodes.source_text: the 1T phase was thermally converted into the 2H phase via annealing under N2 at 800°C. Subsequently, Pt SNDs were in situ grown on the 2H-MoS2, forming 2H-MoS2@Pt heterostructure (Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information) via the same synthesis approach.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm the absence of impurities in 1T-MoS2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Taking 1T-MoS2@Pt as an illustrative example, XRD patterns confirm the absence of impurities (Figure S3, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals uniform dispersion of subnano-sized Pt dots with average size of ≈2.5 nm on 1T-MoS2 surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Figure 1b; Figure S4, Supporting Information) reveal a uniform dispersion of subnano-sized Pt dots with an average size of ≈2.5 nm

properties.features: interconnected spherical nanoparticles forming porous network

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms high crystallinity of 1T-MoS2@Pt with Mo-Mo spacing of 0.537 nm, lattice constants a=b=0.305 nm, and Pt (200) planes at 0.197 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further structural characterization using atomic-scale high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging (Figure 1c) confirms the high crystallinity

nodes.characterization_summary: Geometric phase analysis reveals ≈3% tensile strain (XX/YY) and ≈1.5% shear strain (XY) in curved 1T-MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Geometric phase analysis (GPA) of the HAADF-STEM image (Figure 1g) reveals that curved 1T-MoS2 sustains ≈3% tensile strain (XX/YY directions) and ≈1.5% shear strain (XY direction)

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping indicates homogeneous distribution of Mo, S, and Pt in 1T-MoS2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM-energy-dispersive Xray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping (Figure 1h) indicates a homogeneous distribution of Mo, S, and Pt

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Pt loading as 7.43 wt.% in 1T-MoS2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) determines the Pt loading as 7.43 wt.%

nodes.characterization_summary: 1T-MoS2@Pt shows asymmetric J1,J2,J3 peaks characteristic of metallic 1T phase with 5 cm^-1 downshift; 2H-MoS2@Pt shows symmetric E1_2g and A1g modes with 3 cm^-1 upshift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2a, Raman spectroscopy confirms the preservation of 1T-MoS2 phase integrity after Pt loading, as evidenced by asymmetric vibrational peaks (J1, J2, J3) characteristic of the metallic 1T phase. In contrast, the 2H MoS2@Pt exhibits symmetric E1_2g and A1g modes typical of the semiconducting 2H phase

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis shows minimal absorption for metallic 1T-MoS2 and 1T-MoS2@Pt; 2H-MoS2 and 2H-MoS2@Pt exhibit semiconductor absorption edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV-vis absorption spectra provide additional differentiation between the phases. The monodispersed aqueous solutions of 1T-MoS2 and 1T-MoS2@Pt show minimal absorption due to metallic scattering

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo 3d binding energy shows +0.23 eV upshift in 1T-MoS2@Pt (electron donation to Pt) and -0.17 eV downshift in 2H-MoS2@Pt (electron acceptance from Pt); Pt 4f shows downshift in 1T (electron-enriched) and upshift in 2H (electron-deficient).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS data reveal that metallic 1T-MoS2 donates electrons to as-prepared Pt SNDs (Figure S9, Supporting Information), as evidenced by the +0.23 eV upshift in Mo 3d binding energy upon Pt loading (Figure 2c). In contrast, semiconducting 2H-MoS2 accepts electrons from Pt SNDs, resulting in a -0.17 eV downshift in the Mo 3d binding energy

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES shows weaker white-line intensity for 1T-MoS2@Pt (higher d-electron occupancy) vs 2H-MoS2@Pt (d-electron depletion).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt L3-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis (Figure 2e), which reveals weaker white-line intensity for 1T-MoS2@Pt (higher d-electron occupancy)

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS confirms Pt-S coordination at 1.9 Å and Pt-Pt at 2.6 Å; stronger Pt-S bonding in 1T-MoS2@Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform analysis results of the k3-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) for 1T-/2H-MoS2@Pt. The peak at 2.6 Å... is attributed to Pt-Pt coordination

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals high crystallinity of Rh SNDs (2.7 nm) with (111) lattice spacing of 0.220 nm and Ru SNDs (1.4 nm) with (100) lattice spacing of 0.238 nm on 1T-MoS2 support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images reveal the high crystallinity of Rh and Ru SNDs on the 1T-MoS2 support, with lattice spacings measured at 0.220 nm (Figure S16, Supporting Information) and 0.238 nm (Figure S17, Supporting Information), corresponding to the (111) and (100) planes, respectively
